Suzerain over Upper Nubia above the Third Cataract, including the vassal kingdom of Dongola; Lower Nubia nominally under Ottoman Egypt. 'Abdallab recognised as paramount chiefs of the Arabs; Kordofan contested with Darfur (Holt & Daly, intro pp.5, 8).

Key events
  • King 'Umara Dunqas defeats the 'Abdallabi at Arbaji, 1504 (GHA V ch.7 p.173)
  • Islamisation; Sufi orders introduced from the Hijaz, the Qadiriyya in 1577 (GHA V ch.7 pp.173, 179–180)
  • Turco-Egyptian forces take Sennar, 1821 (GHA V ch.7 p.185)
  • Holt & Daly: Funj suzerainty over Upper Nubia (above 3rd Cataract) incl. vassal-kingdom of Dongola; 'Abdallab recognised as paramount chiefs of the Arabs
  • From about the mid-17th century to 1861 the Shilluk pushed the frontier north to Hays, raiding the Funj sultanate and the Nuba mountains
  • Islamization of the Funj and the Umayyad ancestry claim
  • The Shaykiyya break away from the Funj
  • Funj aristocracy revolts against the slave army; Unsa III deposed
  • Sennar described as Africa's greatest trading city

Capitals / sites: Sennar

Culture

The Fundj were rapidly Islamised (GHA V ch.7 p.173); most Sufi orders were introduced from the Hijaz, the Qadiriyya first, brought to the Djazira in 1577 (GHA V ch.7 pp.179–180); Arab genealogical identity (Ja'ali/'Abbasi, Juhayna) spreading among riverain peoples (Holt & Daly, intro pp.3, 5).

Economy

North–south route Sennar–Egypt and west–east route Darfur–Suakin; Shendi the main market by c.1800; staples millet and dammur cloth used as currency, foreign silver for large deals; slaves of pre-eminent importance in trade (Holt & Daly, intro pp.7–9).

Dating note

1504–1821: Funj victory over the 'Abdallabi at Arbaji in 1504 (GHA V ch.7 p.173); Turco-Egyptian forces take Sennar in 1821 (GHA V ch.7 p.185; GHA VI ch.14 p.356: the Sennar rulers 'capitulated to the Turkish rulers in 1821' after the sultanate's disintegration into 'weak and hostile shaykhdoms'). Foundation by a Shilluk band is a tradition, not established fact [NO-SOURCE: no page read].

الثقافة

انتشار الإسلام والطرق الصوفية؛ وانتشار الهوية النسبية العربية (الجعلية/العباسية، جهينة) بين سكان ضفاف النيل (هولت وديلي، المقدمة ص3، 5). [يحتاج تحقق]

الاقتصاد

طريق شمالي–جنوبي بين سنار ومصر، وطريق غربي–شرقي بين دارفور وسواكن؛ وشندي السوق الرئيسية نحو 1800؛ والذرة وقماش الدمور وسيلتا تبادل، والفضة الأجنبية للصفقات الكبيرة؛ وللرقيق أهمية بارزة في التجارة (هولت وديلي، المقدمة ص7–9).

ملاحظة التأريخ

1504–1821: Funj victory over the 'Abdallabi at Arbaji in 1504 (GHA V ch.7 p.173); Turco-Egyptian forces take Sennar in 1821 (GHA V ch.7 p.185; GHA VI ch.14 p.356: the Sennar rulers 'capitulated to the Turkish rulers in 1821' after the sultanate's disintegration into 'weak and hostile shaykhdoms'). Foundation by a Shilluk band is a tradition, not established fact [NO-SOURCE: no page read]. يحتاج تحقق
